findings.reason: without adding the promotion/observe module(s) to the write paths or naming the caller, a dispatched node is fenced out of the very path its done-when exercises, and the node's blocking report would be re-raised as a defect after dispatch.
findings.text: s12's second mechanism, "A run whose supervisor did not file the record has it filed by the next `crew complete` or `crew observe` of that run", has no named caller and its implementation site is outside the section's declared write paths (`reckon/crew/recovery_review_subject.py`, `reckon/crew/review.py`, `reckon/crew/dispatch_launch.py`, `reckon/crew/dispatch_admission.py`, and the new test): `crew complete` is composed in `reckon/crew/promotion*.py` and `crew observe` in `reckon/crew/dispatch_sessions.py:163`, neither of which the node may write, so the required fallback call cannot be added and the second case's done-when ("the record filed at `review.review_path` after one `crew complete`") is unreachable within the granted scope

— the claim "every reader of the store finds the record where it finds it now, and no reader changes" does not hold for `_review_subject` (`reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py:150`): it recovers the reviewed run *and head* from the declared record paths via `_review_store_record_paths`, which selects a path only when its parent is the store's project directory, so a declaration moved into the run directory is filtered out and the head is lost — `_review_subject` then returns `(_resolved_reviewed_run_id(...), "")`, and `_review_head_covers("", head)` returns True, so a live review that read one revision is treated as covering any later one and the reflex will not dispatch a fresh review after the run advances; WOULD_CHANGE_THE_PLAN: yes — REASON: the repair must either preserve the reviewed head where the reflex reads it or update `recovery_review_dispatch.py`, which is itself absent from the write paths, so the plan as written leaves a reader unchanged in name but regressed in behaviour.

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `c-s10-review-store-gap` resolves (plan.html:2024, carrying the same 4,233-record measurement s12 quotes); `recovery_review_subject.py` "around line 610" resolves (the `review_path(project, run_id)` / `reviewed_head_sha` composition is at :610-:613); `_fence_write_roots` resolves (`reckon/crew/dispatch_admission.py:1842`); `delivery_write_roots` resolves (`reckon/_backends.py:140`); `review.review_path` resolves (`reckon/crew/review.py:1969`); `python -m reckon.crew.supervisor_main` and `_supervisor_exit_record` resolve (`reckon/crew/supervisor_main.py`, `reckon/crew/dispatch_launch.py:2371`); `review_present` resolves (`reckon/crew/recovery_classification.py:1501`).
rubric_items.done_when: pass — the done-when names a measurable outcome (fence composed through the production dispatch path, a fenced sibling-record `rm` exits non-zero, a live read as `review_present`) and two declared negative controls (widen the grant back to the parent directory; remove the fallback filing), each with the red case it must produce.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — gate logs and both negative controls are written "under the run directory" (run-scoped, durable), never a scratchpad, and the report lives at the assigned report path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the section and its new test file (`tests/test_a_run_review_cannot_remove_a_siblings_record.py`) name the mechanism, not a stage, plan label or ticket; the only `s10`-bearing token is the plan-side decision id.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the stated root cause matches the cited evidence, and the seal mechanism does produce the done-when, but two callers/readers the deliverable relies on are outside the plan's account: the fallback filing's caller (`crew complete` / `crew observe`) is not named and lies outside the declared write paths, and a reader `_review_subject` derives the reviewed head from the declared path and changes under the new shape, against the plan's "no reader changes" claim.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — the node carries one deliverable (a run review's fence grants nothing writable that holds another run's record); the run-dir declaration, the supervisor filing and the fallback are the shape of that one outcome, not a second goal.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — s12 declares no unsatisfied dependency: it repairs a gap §10 (status `done`, merged) left, and its write paths name existing modules, so no depends-on or gates edge is missing.
